svg.title: Drawback Claim Economics in Percent
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-04-drawback-claim-economics-bands; chapter number: 2; title: Drawback Claim Economics in Percent; subtitle: Refund rate, unclaimed share, matching uplift and partner incentive; caption: Drawback returns 99% of eligible duties, taxes and fees. Most of the pool goes unclaimed, and optimal substitution matching can lift recovery well beyond greedy logic.; assumptions note: All values are percentages reported by the named speakers. Where a speaker gave a single figure, min, max and typical are equal. Section 232, AD/CVD and over-quota duties are excluded from recovery.; note: Sources are Thompson Hine LLP (Aaron Mandelbaum), Flexport (Monica Pascarella and the drawback team), USA Customs Clearance and World Trade Center Denver.; chart type: horizontal_bars; unit: percent; bars: label: Refund rate on eligible duties, taxes and fees; min: 99; max: 99; typical: 99; display: 99%; label: Retained by customs for administrative fees; min: 1; max: 1; typical: 1; display: 1%; label: Share of eligible drawback left unclaimed; min: 70; max: 80; typical: 70; display: About 70% (Flexport) to 70-80% (USA Customs Clearance); label: Optimized substitution matching uplift; min: 10; max: 400; typical: 35; display: 10-400%, about 35% average; label: Partner cooperation incentive per claim; min: 10; max: 10; typical: 10; display: Something like 10% per claim
